approaches.name: Remove matched pairs repeatedly
approaches.intuition: A valid string always contains an adjacent pair like `()`; removing pairs until nothing changes leaves an empty string exactly when the input is valid.
steps: Stop when no pair is found
Valid if the string is now empty
approaches.time: O(n^2) in the worst case: each pass is linear and there can be n/2 passes
pitfalls: Forgetting that removing one pair can create a new adjacent pair.

approaches.name: Stack of open brackets
approaches.intuition: Only the latest unmatched opener can legally be closed, so keep openers on a stack and match each closer against the top.
steps: On a closer, compare with the top and pop
Empty stack at the end means valid
pitfalls: Popping from an empty stack: check for it before comparing.
Forgetting the final check: `((` never fails mid-way but is not valid.

talkTrackMd: Say that the structure is nested, so the last opened bracket closes first. Name the stack, walk the three failure cases (wrong kind, closer with nothing open, leftover openers), and give the linear complexity.
